title: FDAM ERP: Track Franchise Inquiries from Source to Consultation
description: FDAM issues a unique franchise inquiry link per channel, logs leads automatically, merges duplicates and compares channel conversion rates to guide ad spend.
html:
FDAM, the franchise ERP that standardizes franchisee recruitment data with franchise inquiry links for each lead source

franchise ERP, FDAM, franchise inquiry management, lead source analysis, sales management, franchisee recruitment, lead management, channel performance analysis, HQ operating system, sales automation

Key takeaways

· When franchise inquiries from different channels are collected in Excel, duplicates, omissions and delays keep recurring.

· FDAM issues a unique franchise inquiry link for each lead source and automatically registers inquiries in the sales management module the moment they come in.

· Alert-driven follow-up and duplicate-merging logic reduce both gaps in sales coverage and inflated counts.

· You can compare inquiry volume, time to first contact and conversion rate by channel, moving ad budget decisions onto data.

Franchise inquiry link managementis an operating approach in which franchisor headquarters issue a unique link for each channel, such as Naver Blog, Instagram, the website and banner ads, so that incoming franchise inquiries are automatically logged in the sales management module of the HQ ERP. To compare channel performance on one screen when recruiting franchisees, data must accumulate on the same basis from the moment a lead comes in.

In the field, collecting franchise inquiries from each channel in Excel and then passing them along to staff happens over and over, frequently causing problems such as duplicates, omissions and delays. As the number of franchise stores grows, it becomes harder to answer clearly, "Which channels actually led to consultations and contracts?" FDAM, from MS Venter, which has focused on franchise IT for nearly 25 years, is designed to solve this problem within its sales management module.

Connect lead capture → intake → consultation within a single system.

1. Standardized intake with unique links for each lead source

Each channel gets its own link, and lead source information is recorded automatically.

Once HQ defines the channels it runs, such as Naver Blog, Instagram, the website and offline events, a unique link is issued for each one. The moment a prospective franchisee submits a consultation request through that link, the inquiry is organized through a standard process and added to FDAM's intake and consultation list.

Because lead source information is recorded along with each inquiry, you can compare inquiry flow by channel and campaign right away, without separate consolidation. As soon as a new inquiry arrives, the sales team can quickly kick off its routine of assigning an owner → first contact → booking a consultation.

As a result, HQ can adjust budgets, messaging and creative based on data, and the sales team in the field can prioritize the leads most likely to convert.

2. Reducing gaps with alert-driven follow-up

New inquiries trigger instant alerts and are assigned automatically based on routing rules.

With alerts set up, staff receive a real-time notification the moment a new inquiry comes in. Time to first contact shortens, and work distribution is automated according to the team lead's routing rules.

For leads whose conversion to consultation is delayed, overdue alerts repeat based on their status (e.g., Not contacted / Needs follow-up / On hold), reducing the number of leads that slip through the cracks. Duplicate-merging logic(based on phone number, email, input patterns and more) groups repeat inquiries from the same person into one, preventing the illusion of inflated counts, and consultation history and comments can be viewed together on one screen, easing the burden of handovers.

When lead capture, intake and consultation flow without breaks, the sales team doesn't spend time checking "who did what, and when," and can focus on consultation quality and conversion strategy. The HQ sales workflow distilled from our experience working with about 500 brands is built directly into the module's design, so the system fits naturally into the way HQ sales teams already work.

3. Making ad budget decisions by comparing channel performance

Key metrics for each lead source accumulate in a standardized form.

The benefits of using data are clearest when comparing channels. By comparing key metrics such as inquiry volume, average time to first contact and consultation booking rate by lead source, you can quickly decide where to invest more within the same budget.

For example, if inquiries from Naver Blog have a higher consultation booking rate than Instagram but take longer to receive a first contact, that points to concrete actions such as adjusting response hours for that channel or optimizing the required fields on the inquiry form. Conversely, if the offline event link brings in a lot of leads, you can organize follow-up remarketing messages as templates in the ERP and standardize your follow-up campaigns.

What matters is that all of these decisions are based on standardized data inside the franchise ERP. Even when report formats change, the definitions behind the numbers stay the same, so they hold steady through staff changes and reorganizations. Ask the AI assistant, the first to be built into a Korean franchise ERP, "Compare conversion rates by channel for last quarter," and you'll instantly get an answer organized as tables and charts.

4. Expected benefits of franchise inquiry link management

Visible ad performance · Stronger sales connectivity · Better operational efficiency.

The expected benefits of franchise inquiry link management come down to three things.

Three expected benefits

① Visible ad performance — Inquiry counts and conversion metrics by lead source are tallied automatically, revealing budget efficiency.

② Stronger sales connectivity — Instant alerts and routing on intake speed up first responses, boosting the chances of signing a contract.

③ Better operational efficiency — Less time spent on manual consolidation, deduplication and report editing, and weekly and monthly reviews move faster with standardized data.

Now channel managers, sales leaders and executives can talk using the same screen and the same numbers. If the goal of adopting an HQ system goes beyond "easier management" to "a foundation for growth," franchise inquiry link management is the most practical place to start.

Frequently asked questions

Q. Is there a limit to the number of franchise inquiry links we can issue?

HQ can issue and run as many links as it needs, by channel, campaign or ad creative. The more finely you segment channels, the more precise your channel comparisons become, but splitting them too finely can clutter your analysis, so it's best to set the level of detail to suit your HQ's operating environment.

Q. If the same person inquires through multiple channels, won't it be counted twice?

FDAM runs duplicate-merging logic based on phone number, email, input patterns and more. Repeat inquiries from the same person are grouped and managed as a single lead, while the history of which channel they first came from is preserved, so channel performance analysis remains undistorted.

Q. At what level can alerts be configured?

Alerts can be set for each stage, such as new inquiry intake, owner assignment and overdue follow-ups. If you design routing and alert conditions together to match your HQ's sales operating rules, system alerts will flow exactly the way your sales team works.

Q. Do we need to run it separately from our existing ad systems?

Keep running your ads on your existing channels, and simply link the franchise inquiry links issued by FDAM to your ad creatives. There's no need to adopt a new ad management system; only the sales flow after a lead comes in is managed in one place within FDAM.
